title: Surface blocker cause, dependency waits and human-review flag on IDE task cards
description:
Roadmap 2026-09-10 §4 "Visible parked work" and the Wave 0 row "blocker visibility". A parked task is currently indistinguishable from live work in both IDE clients, so finding out why anything stopped requires a chat search.

The daemon already persists every field needed: packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts declares needsHumanReview (line 727), blockedReason (741), blockedResourceId (757), blockedOnTaskIds (767), blockedFromStatus (769) and blockedAt (771). Neither client reads any of them. moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/model/Models.kt:111 `data class Task` has no blocker field at all, and grepping the whole Kotlin source for blockedReason/needsHumanReview/blockedOnTaskIds returns nothing. moe-vscode/src/types/moe.ts is the same. Because BLOCKED is display-mapped into the Working column, a task parked on a resource lease, a dependency wait or an external blocker renders as an ordinary in-progress card with no cause and no indication of what will clear it.

Scope: parse those fields into the JetBrains Task model, give a BLOCKED card a distinct badge that names the cause (dependency wait, resource wait, plain external block, awaiting human review), and show blockedReason plus the blockedOnTaskIds prerequisites in task detail. Distinguish the three causes, since each clears differently: a dependency wait clears when its prerequisites reach DONE, a resource wait clears on lease grant, and a plain block needs a human. Do not add a board column and do not change any daemon behaviour or lifecycle rule; this is a read-only display change over state the daemon already sends.
definitionOfDone: moe-jetbrains Task model parses needsHumanReview, blockedReason, blockedOnTaskIds, blockedResourceId, blockedFromStatus and blockedAt from the daemon payload, with a MoeJsonTest case asserting a BLOCKED task round-trips all six
A BLOCKED card in the Working column renders a distinct badge naming the cause: dependency wait, resource wait, external block, or awaiting human review
Task detail shows the blockedReason text and lists the blockedOnTaskIds prerequisites
needsHumanReview renders its own attention badge independent of BLOCKED status
A JUnit test covers the cause-selection logic for all four cases and fails on the old behaviour (today every BLOCKED task renders as a plain Working card)
VS Code parity lands in this task only if trivial; otherwise a follow-up card is filed and named in the completion summary
taskRails: Display only: do not change report_blocked, the auto-unblock paths, nextStatusForRelease or any daemon lifecycle rule.
Do not add a sixth board column; BLOCKED stays display-mapped into Working.
Keep the cause badge derived from a pure, headless-testable function so JUnit can assert it without an IDE fixture.

implementationPlan.description: CREATE THE PURE PRESENTATION FUNCTION AND ITS MESSAGE KEYS. New file moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/TaskBlockerPresentation.kt containing a headless object with no Swing and no IntelliJ imports, so JUnit can assert it with no IDE fixture - that is an explicit task rail. Declare the data types at TOP LEVEL in that file, never inside a companion object, because a classifier nested in a companion is not importable as Outer.Inner and has already cost this repo a failed build. Types: `enum class BlockCause { RESOURCE_WAIT, DEPENDENCY_WAIT, EXTERNAL_BLOCK }`; a badges result carrying a nullable cause plus an independent needsHumanReview flag; and a detail result carrying the cause, the reason, the recorded prerequisite ids, the resource id, blockedFromStatus, blockedAt and the attention flag. THE RULES, which mirror daemon behavior rather than inventing policy. A cause is derived ONLY while status equals BLOCKED; for every other status the cause is null and no active-block detail is offered, so leftover metadata on a task that has moved on can never render as a live block. Within BLOCKED the order is fixed: a non-blank blockedResourceId gives RESOURCE_WAIT, else a list holding at least one non-blank id gives DEPENDENCY_WAIT, else EXTERNAL_BLOCK. Resource wins because the daemon's dependency auto-unblock deliberately skips resource-waiting rows and the lease grant clears all block metadata, so a row carrying both is really waiting on the lease. needsHumanReview is fully independent: it is honoured whenever the flag is true, including on REVIEW and on a task that is not blocked at all, and it is NEVER inferred from status, from the reason text or from a critique result. Error handling, all of it returning a value rather than throwing, because this runs inside paint and refresh paths: a missing or blank reason yields a localized fallback; blank and whitespace-only prerequisite ids are filtered out while the remaining ids keep their recorded order and duplicates; blockedAt is passed through exactly as sent with no date parsing; no input shape may throw. Add the message keys to moe-jetbrains/src/main/resources/messages/MoeBundle.properties: one short badge label per cause, one attention badge label, one clearance explanation per cause phrased as what will clear it - prerequisites reaching a finished state for a dependency wait, a lease grant for a resource wait, a person for an external block - a reason-missing fallback, and a heading for the prerequisite list. Word the prerequisite list as the ids the task RECORDED as waited on, not as unfinished work, because the daemon also treats archived and deleted ids as satisfied.
implementationPlan.note:
NEW FILE `moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/TaskBlockerPresentation.kt` (192 lines). Imports exactly one thing: `com.moe.model.Task`. No Swing, no IntelliJ, no clock, no daemon call — headless per the task rail.

TOP-LEVEL declarations (never inside a companion, per the plan's build-failure warning):
- `enum class BlockCause(val badgeKey: String, val clearanceKey: String) { RESOURCE_WAIT, DEPENDENCY_WAIT, EXTERNAL_BLOCK }`
- `data class TaskBlockerBadges(cause: BlockCause?, needsHumanReview: Boolean)` with a `hasAny` convenience getter
- `data class TaskBlockerDetail(cause, reason, reasonFallbackKey, prerequisiteIds, resourceId, fromStatus, blockedAt, needsHumanReview)`
- `object TaskBlockerPresentation` with `cause(task)`, `badges(task)`, `detail(task)`, `prerequisiteIds(task)`, `allMessageKeys()`.

DESIGN DECISION forced by step 1's measurement: the presentation emits MoeBundle **KEYS**, not localized text, because `MoeBundle` wraps `com.intellij.DynamicBundle` and a headless JUnit test cannot resolve a message. This matches the existing `TaskDetailDialog.KpiRow.labelKey` precedent. The Swing callers do the `MoeBundle.message(...)` lookup. `allMessageKeys()` enumerates every emittable key (9 object constants + both keys of each of the 3 enum values = 15) so step 3's Properties guard cannot rot.

RULES IMPLEMENTED:
- Cause derived ONLY while `status == "BLOCKED"`; any other status gives null cause AND a detail with every block field empty. Stale metadata on a moved-on task can never render as a live block.
- Within BLOCKED, fixed order: non-blank `blockedResourceId` -> RESOURCE_WAIT; else at least one non-blank id in `blockedOnTaskIds` -> DEPENDENCY_WAIT; else EXTERNAL_BLOCK. Resource wins (daemon dependency auto-unblock skips resource-waiting rows; the lease grant clears all block metadata).
- `needsHumanReview` is read verbatim off the model and honoured on ANY status, including REVIEW and unblocked tasks. Never inferred from status, reason text or critique verdict. `detail()` returns a non-null attention-only result when the flag is true on a non-blocked task.
- Error handling, all value-returning (runs in paint/refresh paths, so nothing throws): blank/missing reason -> `reason = null` + `reasonFallbackKey = "moe.blocker.reason.missing"` (set exactly when there is a live block and no usable reason); blank/whitespace ids filtered out, survivors keep recorded order + duplicates + exact bytes; `blockedAt` passed through with no date parsing (blank suppressed to null, same for `resourceId`/`fromStatus`); `blockedOnTaskIds` null and a real `[]` both collapse to an empty prerequisite list, which is correct because both mean "no usable dependency".

BUNDLE: appended 15 keys + a 2-line comment header to `MoeBundle.properties` (was 219 lines, now 236). File is **LF, not CRLF** (measured: 0 CRLF, 219 LF) so the append used LF. All new values are pure ASCII on purpose — `java.util.Properties.load(InputStream)` decodes ISO-8859-1, so a non-ASCII value would read back as mojibake in the guard test (the pre-existing `Refreshing…` entries already have that 12-byte non-ASCII quirk; untouched). Clearance strings are phrased as what clears them: lease grant / prerequisites reaching DONE or ARCHIVED / a person. `moe.blocker.prerequisites=Prerequisites recorded as waited on` deliberately avoids claiming the ids are unfinished, since the daemon counts archived and deleted ids as satisfied.

No test run in this step (step 3 owns the focused run). Foreign dirty paths `docs/MCP_SERVER.md` and `docs/SCHEMA.md` still untouched.

implementationPlan.description: COVER THE PRESENTATION WITH HEADLESS JUNIT. New file moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/TaskBlockerPresentationTest.kt, JUnit 4 in the style of the existing MetricsPanelTest - plain assertions against the production function, no IDE fixture, no daemon. Assert exact enum values and exact strings, never bare truthiness. Cases: each of the three causes in isolation; a BLOCKED task carrying a resource id AND prerequisite ids AND the attention flag resolves to RESOURCE_WAIT with attention still true, which is the precedence proof; a BLOCKED task with neither a resource nor usable ids is an EXTERNAL_BLOCK; an ordinary task with no metadata has a null cause and no attention. Empty and missing shapes: a null dependency list, a real empty list, a list of only blank strings, and a blank or whitespace resource id each fall through to the next branch correctly. Staleness: a WORKING or REVIEW task still carrying populated blocker fields yields a null cause and no active-block detail, while its attention flag survives - then walk a single task through BLOCKED, WORKING and REVIEW and assert attention persists until the flag itself clears. Data fidelity: prerequisite ids keep their recorded order and duplicates, a multiline reason and a very long reason survive verbatim, and a missing or blank reason yields the localized fallback. Add a guard test that loads /messages/MoeBundle.properties from the test classpath with java.util.Properties and asserts every key the presentation can emit is defined, so a missing localization fails the build instead of shipping a raw placeholder. Run the focused class - Windows from the repository root `& .\moe-jetbrains\gradlew.bat -p moe-jetbrains test --tests com.moe.toolwindow.TaskBlockerPresentationTest; exit $LASTEXITCODE`, Unix `(cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test --tests com.moe.toolwindow.TaskBlockerPresentationTest)` - and require green with nonzero counts. implementationPlan.description: SHOW THE CAUSE, REASON AND PREREQUISITES IN TASK DETAIL. Edit moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/TaskDetailDialog.kt only. Add one read-only blocker section that appears only when the presentation reports a cause or the attention flag, showing the localized cause label and its clearance explanation, the reason text, the recorded prerequisite ids, and the resource id and blockedFromStatus and blockedAt when present. Render every daemon-supplied string as LITERAL PLAIN TEXT: use a read-only wrapping text area or a plain-text label, and do not build a markup string around reason or id content the way the comment renderer in PlanReviewDialog does - a blockedReason is arbitrary agent output and must never be interpreted as markup. New fields beside the plan ones: `private var blockerContainer: JPanel? = null` and `private val log = Logger.getInstance(TaskDetailDialog::class.java)`. 3. The **existing single** listener's `onState` now refreshes both sections: `safeRefresh("plan panel") { refreshPlanPanel(updated) }` then `safeRefresh("blocker section") { refreshBlockerSection(updated) }`. The `state.tasks.find { it.id == task.id } ?: return` early return for a task that vanished is untouched. **No second listener was added** and `dispose()` is unchanged — still the single removal point. 4. The section is mounted directly under the status line in `createCenterPanel` (a `JPanel(BorderLayout())` wrapper held in `blockerContainer`, populated from `buildBlockerPanel(task)` which returns null when there is nothing to show). Placed there because "why did this stop" is the question a parked card raises. 5. New private members: `buildBlockerPanel`, `headline`, `explanation`, `literalText`, `refreshBlockerSection`, `safeRefresh`. All under 50 lines except `buildBlockerPanel` (~55 incl. KDoc/blank lines; body is a flat sequence of optional rows). WHAT IT SHOWS (only when `TaskBlockerPresentation.detail(task)` is non-null, i.e. a live cause or the attention flag): the localized cause label + its clearance explanation; the `moe.blocker.reason` caption with the reason text, falling back to the localized `reasonFallbackKey` when the daemon sent none; the attention headline + explanation when the flag is true; the `moe.blocker.prerequisites` caption with the recorded ids one per line; and a compact facts block with resource id, blockedFromStatus and blockedAt, each rendered only when present. MARKUP SAFETY (the load-bearing rail): every daemon-supplied string goes through `literalText()`, a read-only wrapping `JBTextArea` in a borderless `JScrollPane` — the same shape as the existing read-only reopenReason area. This matters more than the plan assumed: Swing's `JLabel` itself interprets a string beginning with an html tag, so even a plain `JBLabel` would have been unsafe. `JBLabel` is used ONLY for `MoeBundle` text. Nothing in this section builds a markup string the way the comment renderer at line 177 does (`JBLabel("${comment.content...}")`) — that hazard was deliberately not copied. A test fixture already proves the presentation passes `not markup` through verbatim. LIVE CLEAR ON UNBLOCK: `refreshBlockerSection` mirrors `refreshPlanPanel` — `SwingUtilities.invokeLater { removeAll(); buildBlockerPanel(updated)?.let { add(it) }; revalidate(); repaint() }`. An unblocked task simply finds no detail to build, so the section empties itself with no reopen.
